overlap_rationale: Study A (S311) has a complete, readable full text examining resource allocation in Tanzania's Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Program (RWSSP) using national ministry interviews/documents, district budget allocation data, an analysis of 40 first-phase RWSSP projects (10 per district), and fieldwork conducted between July 2008 and August 2009 in four rural districts (Iramba, Nzega, Kigoma Rural and Same, with deeper ward/village fieldwork in Same and Nzega). Study A explicitly cites Study B as 'Jime´nez and Pe´rez-Foguet 2010b' on PDF pages 11 and 12 when discussing processes needed for village-level water information to influence Local Government Authority (LGA) priorities, indicating that both papers stem from the same authors' research programme on rural water governance in Tanzania. However, Study B (S315) has no accessible full text ('[FULL TEXT NOT ACCESSIBLE — NO VERIFIED FULL-TEXT PDF COULD BE RETRIEVED]'). Without Study B's full text, we cannot verify its exact districts, fieldwork dates, respondent groups, sample size, or empirical tables, and therefore cannot determine whether S311 and S315 analyze the exact same fieldwork sample, partially overlapping district/mapping data, or distinct samples.
study_a_sample_and_data: Multi-level qualitative and administrative study of Tanzania's Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Program (RWSSP) combining Ministry of Water and PMO-RALG official interviews and national budget/coverage records (across 132 districts) with fieldwork conducted between July 2008 and August 2009 in 4 rural districts (Iramba, Nzega, Kigoma Rural and Same). Includes interviews with District Water Engineers and District Planning Officers, evaluation of 40 Phase 1 RWSSP village projects (10 per district), in-depth fieldwork in 4 wards across 2 districts (Mwakashanhala and Itobo in Nzega; Myamba and Hedaru in Same) involving ward/village/subvillage leaders, government officers, village plans and randomly selected villagers, plus brief interviews with ward officers in 50% of Same wards selected randomly.
study_b_sample_and_data: Full text not accessible. Citation metadata indicates a 2010 Natural Resources Forum article (34(2):93-105) by the same authors on Local Government Authorities and the human right to water in rural Tanzania, but the specific districts, fieldwork dates, sample size (N), respondent groups and empirical datasets cannot be verified.
